name: Hashcat - Hash Mode Reference
description: The -m mode number tells hashcat which algorithm the hash is. Getting it wrong makes cracking silently fail, so identify the hash first (hashid) then match the mode. These are the ones the module uses; the full list is in the example-hashes wiki.

examples.label: Crack a Linux sha512crypt shadow hash

notes:
Look modes up with `hashcat --help | grep -i <algo>` or the example_hashes wiki. Wrong -m = no cracks and no error.
Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 19 (Password Attacks)

recommended.note: Identify the hash before picking a mode.
Run the crack once you know the mode.

variations.label: General hashes
variations.command:
0     - MD5
100   - SHA1
1400  - SHA2-256
1700  - SHA2-512
900   - MD4
500   - MD5 Crypt / Cisco-IOS(MD5) / FreeBSD MD5
1800  - sha512crypt (Linux $6$ shadow)
3200  - bcrypt $2*$ (Blowfish)
6000  - RIPEMD-160
600   - BLAKE2b-512

variations.label: Windows / AD
variations.command:
1000  - NT (NTLM)
3000  - LM
5500  - NetNTLMv1
5600  - NetNTLMv2
2100  - DCC2 (Domain Cached Credentials 2 / MS Cache 2)
13100 - Kerberoast (TGS-REP, etc/RC4)
18200 - AS-REP roast (RC4)

variations.label: Files / disks
variations.command:
22100 - BitLocker
13400 - KeePass
11600 - 7-Zip
13000 - RAR5
17210 - PKZIP
9400  - MS Office 2007
9600  - MS Office 2013
10500 - PDF 1.4-1.6
